Resolving damage once an attack hits (SR2 p.91). Also called the Damage Resistance Test.

1 · Roll to resist

  • Target number = the weapon's Power Rating − the armor rating the character is wearing. Any result below 2 counts as 2.
  • Dice = Body, plus any Combat Pool dice committed. Roll Combat Pool dice in a different colour — you need to know how many of them succeeded, separately from the total.
  • Rule of One and Rule of Six apply as normal.

2 · Compare successes and stage the damage

(L)ight — (M)oderate — (S)erious — (D)eadly
stage up one level per 2 net successes →    ← stage down one level per 2 net successes

ResultEffect
Attacker rolls more successesdamage rises one level per 2 full net successes
Successes are equalthe weapon does its base Damage Level
Target rolls more successesdamage drops one level per 2 full net successes
Damage falls below Lightno damage
Target's Combat Pool dice alone beat the attacker's successescomplete miss

Book example: Snot has Body 5 and 5 points of ballistic armor; Liam fires an Ares Predator (9M). Snot's target number is 4 (9 − 5). Liam scores 5 successes to Snot's 3 — 2 net, enough to stage 9M up to 9S. Had Snot beaten Liam by 2, he'd have staged it down to Light; by 4, no damage at all.

3 · Apply it

Record the result on the target's Condition Monitor (p.111), then check knockdown.

Stopping and Knockdown (SR2 p.91). A character struck by a ranged weapon may be knocked off their feet by the blow.

The test

  • Body Test against a target number equal to one-half the Power of the attack, rounded down.
  • Beat the Threshold Number — one-half the damage done — and there is no effect.
Wound takenThreshold to stay put
Light1
Moderate2
Serious3

Outcomes

ResultWhat happens
Successes exceed the thresholdno effect — the character shrugs it off
Some successes, but not enoughstays standing, but is driven a step or two (one metre) away from the direction of the attack
No successes at allknocked down — the character falls prone

So a character carrying a Moderate wound must generate more than 2 successes to stand their ground.

Damage cards in this system carry a Knockdown Test button that works this out for you.
